newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BIGGIO THREE-RUN TRIPLE GIVES KILE 15TH WIN FOR ASTROS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BIGGIO THREE-RUN TRIPLE GIVES KILE 15TH WIN FOR ASTROS.

text.p: Craig Biggio's three-run triple in the eighth inning made a winner out of Darryl Kile for the 15th time this season as the Houston Astros beat the St Louis Cardinals 7-4 Wednesday for their 11th victory in 12 games.
With the bases loaded and one out in the eighth, Biggio snapped a 4-4 tie by driving a 1-1 pitch from Mark Petkovsek into the right-field corner to clear the bases.
It was the sixth triple of the season for Biggio, who went 7-for-12 with five RBI and four runs scored in the three-game series.
"I was just trying to get the ball out to the outfield, and I did better than that," Biggio said. "I was excited about it when I got to third. It's a nice feeling to come through like that."

Kile (15-3) became the National League's second 15-game winner. He allowed four runs over eight innings to match Greg Maddux for the league lead in wins with his seventh straight victory. The right-hander walked one and struck out seven.
In the month of July, the Astros' ace went 6-0 with a 1.59 ERA, three complete games and two shutouts. Since May 4th, Kile has posted a 14-1 record with five complete games.
Houston has rolled to a 15-4 record since the All-Star break and enjoyed their best July ever, going 19-7.
At Colorado, Andres Galarraga homered twice and Ellis Burks added a two-run shot in his first game back from the disabled list as the Rockies cruised to a 12-6 victory over the Montreal Expos.

Galarraga opened the scoring with a two-out shot in the first off starter Jeff Juden (11-5). With the Rockies ahead 9-6 in the eighth, Galarraga smacked a three-run blast off reliever Rick DeHart to cap the scoring for his 19th career two-homer game.
In two starts in Colorado this season, Juden has been torched for nine earned runs and 13 hits over 4 1/3 innings.
At Florida, rookie Livan Hernandez allowed three hits over eight innings with a career-high eight strikeouts and Moises Alou belted a three-run homer as the Marlins blanked the Cincinnati Reds 6-0.
Hernandez (5-0) walked just two batters as he won his fifth straight start in his longest career outing. He became the first Marlins hurler to get off to a 5-0 start.
Alou hit his 14th homer in the first inning to give the Marlins a 3-0 lead and added an RBI double in the third as Pete Schourek (5-7) lost his third straight start.

In Atlanta, Fred McGriff's one-out single in the bottom of the ninth inning scored Chipper Jones with the winning run as the Braves blew a four-run lead before rallying for a 6-5 victory over the Chicago Cubs.

Danny Bautista led off the ninth with a triple off closer Mel Rojas (0-4) and Jones doubled down the right-field line, scoring Bautista with the tying run. McGriff followed with a single between first and second to bring Jones home.
Alan Embree (3-1) pitched a scoreless ninth to pick up the win for Atlanta after Braves starter John Smoltz struck out 10 over six innings.

In San Francisco, Rick Reed pitched seven strong innings to win his third straight start and Carl Everett had a two-run single in the eighth inning to lift the New York Mets to a 5-2 victory over the Giants.
Reed (9-4), who has gone 5-0 in his last eight starts, gave up two runs and five hits with three walks.
The Giants took a 2-0 lead into the eighth inning but the Mets cut the deficit to 2-1 on Edgardo Alfonzo's RBI single and grabbed the lead on Everett's two-run hit.
New York added a pair of insurance runs in the ninth for their major-league leading 31st come-from-behind win.
Julian Tavarez (3-3) took the loss.
